bottleneck: There is no agreed test for consciousness in non-human animals: behavioral markers like the mirror test and metacognition paradigms are contested, and neural markers derived from humans — global workspace ignition, integrated information — may not transfer across species with radically different brains. This leaves animal welfare, research ethics, and the moral status of cephalopods, corvids, and mammals resting on guesswork. Billions of animals are used in research and agriculture under ethical frameworks that assume an unmeasured property, and the question of which species merit protection cannot be answered without measuring what we cannot yet measure.
current_state: Integrated Information Theory and Global Workspace markers are proposed for animals, but none is validated or consensus-accepted, and cross-species comparisons remain speculative.

title: No validated test for animal consciousness
why_it_blocks: Animal ethics currently runs on intuition and anatomy. A real test of animal consciousness would rewrite research regulations, farming practices, and conservation priorities — but the instrument does not exist.
